why: Cloudflare Workers allow 50 subrequests per request on the free plan (1000 on paid). Every kv.get, kv.put, kv.delete, kv.list and each matching r2 call is one. A request that exceeds it does not slow down — its later calls are refused, and a RAID write loses the tail of its shares. That is how qpu.uuidna.com came to hold feed records with faces 7, 8 and 9 absent.
rule: MAY ONLY SHRINK. Each recorded figure is exact: a door that costs more fails the suite, and a door that costs less fails too, asking for the number to be lowered. A ceiling nobody lowers stops being a measurement. Same discipline as the sibling package's lean-fakes-baseline.json.

profiles.empty: no keys at all. Reads miss, so the store falls back to rebuilding a value from its fourteen shares — which is why an empty store can cost MORE than a full one. The floor a door pays before it pays for any content.
profiles.populated: 256 links with all their shares present, the shape of the live store. THIS is the profile that catches a cost scaling with the store, and an empty-store baseline alone does not: a byte sample over zero keys reads nothing, so it cannot regress.

redundancy_facts.determined: A referrer is a function of its inode. The inode's links carries the key the referrer belongs to, and the address and occupancy are the inode's own, so the pointer holds nothing of its own. Fourteen shares of a derivable document protect nothing.
redundancy_facts.mirrored: The two RAID teams are the same stripes dealt twice, so seven shares determine the value and reading fourteen reads twice what the answer needs.

raid.proof: Held over every residue of length against rays rather than one sampled string: a redundancy claim true of one value is a coincidence, and one true of every residue class is the property (qpuStorageRedundancyHolds).

over.PUT /storage/:key: 91 against a budget of 50, on the populated profile. A deposit writes the inode and the referrer, and each places the value plus fourteen RAID shares across KV and R2. That is 60 subrequests (30 per put) against a budget of 50, leaving a debt of 41. RECONCILIATION WITH RAID REDUNDANCY FACTS: The determined and mirrored facts prove the referrer's shares are derived from the inode and the two teams are identical. This structural property could justify reducing redundancy for referrers, moving this from a discovered problem toward an optimization grounded in RAID theory. This remains a known debt with a number on it because solving it requires deciding whether to change what RAID means — removing redundancy from determined shares — rather than a typical bug fix.

rerecord: QPU_BASELINE=print node --test dist/quantum/processing/unit/raid.test.js — prints the measured table, so lowering a figure is a copy rather than a guess. RAID redundancy facts verified by: node scripts/performance-baseline.mjs
